'How to improve sales forecast accuracy' (guide, Sales Reporting, Dashboards & Forecasting pillar, global; the process discipline behind forecast accuracy, forecast category criteria, deal-level inspection, stage-specific win rates, a weekly cadence and a variance log, distinct from revops-metrics.html (broader RevOps KPI list, not forecast-process specific) and pipeline-automation.html (CRM stage-gate and staleness-alert mechanics, not forecast category discipline or inspection); Miller Heiman Group's CSO Insights 2019 World-Class Sales Practices Study cited (half of all forecasted deals don't close as predicted) and Clari's forecasting research cited (93% of companies can't forecast their number within 5%, even two weeks out); up-linked to the live pillar (sales-dashboards.html) and the live money page (revenue-operations.html), since the record's named money page (sales-forecasting-service) is not live; a worked illustrative twelve-person SaaS team scenario (a 22% commit-to-actual miss narrowed to 9% over two quarters via written commit criteria, a weekly call and a variance log) and a stated practitioner rule (per-rep accuracy tracked separately from the aggregate, since sandbagging and over-committing both distort the number and can cancel each other out in the team total); 1,567 words against the 1,650 guide target, above the 1,500 floor. 'A go-to-market strategy for startups' (guide, Go-to-Market Strategy pillar, global; a sequential, practical guide for an early-stage founder building a first GTM plan, define the buyer precisely, pick one channel from evidence, bound a test with a go/no-go metric decided in advance, scale only after repeatable proof, distinct from types-of-go-to-market-strategies.html (a taxonomy of GTM motions, product-led/sales-led/channel-led) and go-to-market-motion.html (explains the motion concept generally), neither of which sequences the startup-stage validate-before-scale decision this post is built around; CB Insights' 2024 analysis of 431 failed venture-backed companies cited (43% cite poor product-market fit) and the Startup Genome Project's analysis of over 3,200 high-growth startups cited (premature scaling behind the majority of high-growth startup failures; properly-scaled startups grow roughly 20 times faster); up-linked to the live pillar (go-to-market-strategy.html) and the live money page (growth-consulting.html), since the record's named money page (go-to-market-strategy-consulting) is not live; a worked illustrative early-stage B2B SaaS founder scenario (a planned outbound motion shelved in favour of a partner-referral channel that manual testing showed actually converted) and a stated practitioner rule (don't hire into a channel you haven't proven manually, at least a dozen genuine attempts, yourself); 1,579 words against the 1,650 guide target, above the 1,500 floor. 'Form optimisation to lift conversions' (how-to, Conversion & Funnel Optimisation pillar, UK target market; forms specifically, field count, order, type, validation and trust signal, distinct from improve-b2b-website-conversion.html, which covers a whole B2B page across five changes with a form as only one of them, not a dedicated field-level audit; HubSpot's analysis of tens of thousands of customer landing pages cited (three-field forms convert at roughly 25%, each additional field costs an average of 4.1% of conversion, forms with seven or fewer fields convert at 34% against 15% for ten-plus fields); up-linked to the live pillar (conversion-rate-optimisation.html) and the live money page (conversion-rate-optimisation-services.html), both already live, no substitution needed; HowTo schema added (seven ordered steps) alongside Article, FAQPage and BreadcrumbList, per the record's schema_required; a worked illustrative UK B2B software demo-request form scenario (nine fields cut to four, submissions roughly doubling in line with the field-count research, a qualifying dropdown replacing budget and company-size fields as a more honest signal) and a stated practitioner rule (don't ask a visitor for anything you can find out another way, such as company size from a work email domain); 1,575 words against the 1,700 how-to target, above the 1,500 floor.
